title: open-crap4j v1 build
description:
The ordered implementation plan for open-crap4j v1, produced by wayfinder map crap-diy (ticket crap-diy.7). Every design decision is locked, build sessions execute, they do not re-decide.

## Standing rules for every child bead

- Read CONTEXT.md first, its vocabulary is binding.
- TDD is mandatory, use the /tdd skill. Red, green, refactor.
- The locked specs live in research/. Where a spec says it supersedes a section of research/crap4j-research-findings.md, the superseded section must not be followed (notably 5.1 json, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5 are all superseded).
- ADRs in docs/adr/ are binding, JaCoCo XML is the only input, zero runtime dependencies in core and gradle-plugin, one gate reads one report.
- Annotation-based exclusion was dropped from v1 by the crap-diy.7 amendment in research/cli-spec.md, exclusions are path globs and class regexes only.
- Work the beads in dependency order, br ready shows what is next.

The terminal bead gates mcp-contrast end to end. v1 is done when it closes.

title: Scaffold the multi-project build
description:
## Goal
The empty repo becomes the locked three-module Gradle build, green on ./gradlew build.

## Spec
research/build-layout-spec.md, all of it. It supersedes the layout notes in research-findings 5.4.

## Scope
- settings.gradle.kts, rootProject.name open-crap4j, modules core, cli, gradle-plugin. Kotlin DSL throughout. Latest stable wrapper.
- buildSrc convention plugin crap4j.java-conventions: Java toolchain 21, options.release = 17, JUnit 5 + AssertJ test wiring, JaCoCo applied with the XML report forced on.
- Zero-dependency check task (ADR 0002) in the convention plugin, resolves runtimeClasspath and fails on any non-project artifact, wired into check on all three modules.
- gradle.properties version 0.1.0, shared. base.archivesName crap4j-core, crap4j-cli, crap4j-gradle-plugin. Jar manifests carry Implementation-Version.
- gradle-plugin applies java-gradle-plugin with a functionalTest source set registered through gradlePlugin.testSourceSets (tests come later, the wiring lands now).
- Apache-2.0 LICENSE file, .gitignore.

## TDD
The zero-dependency check is the testable behavior. Write a failing functional test (TestKit or a scripted test build) that adds a real external runtime dependency and asserts the check task fails, then make it pass. Plain scaffold files are config, not code, no tests owed.

## Acceptance
- ./gradlew build green with empty module sources.
- The zero-dep test proves the check fires on a non-project runtime artifact and passes clean modules.
- java -jar output of any built jar manifest shows Implementation-Version 0.1.0.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text: Implemented in commit 3ef6886. Added the Gradle 9.6.1 three-module build, shared Java conventions, zero-runtime-dependency enforcement, TestKit coverage on Gradle 8.5 and 9.6.1, artifact/version manifests, wrapper, license, and ignore rules. Verified with ./gradlew build; code review passed Standards and Spec with zero remaining findings.

title: CLI: verbs, flags, exit codes, fat jar
description:
## Goal
The crap4j command ships, four verbs over core, hand-rolled parsing, locked exit codes.

## Spec
research/cli-spec.md, all of it, including the crap-diy.7 amendment (no --exclude-annotation). It supersedes research-findings 5.3, which must not be followed (no --format, no --output, no --write-baseline, no --format none).

## Scope
- Verbs check, report, baseline, tighten mirroring the Gradle tasks. Per-verb flag table verbatim, shared analysis flags on all four. --report is required with NO default path.
- Every refusal from the spec exits 1: changed-files on baseline/tighten, require-tight-baseline with changed-files (check AND report), explicit --baseline that does not exist (check/report), tighten with no baseline, duplicated scalar flags.
- Exit codes 0/1/2, exit 2 exactly when the JSON status is fail. report/baseline/tighten use only 0 and 1. Warnings never change exit codes.
- Output channels: text report to stdout, --json-report <path|-> (dash writes JSON to stdout and suppresses text), --junit-report <path>, diagnostics to stderr (outdated-report, coupled-threshold, baseline config-mismatch warnings).
- Baseline path convention: crap4j-baseline.json in the working directory when present, baseline-less when not, explicit paths must exist.
- Outdated-report warning (CLI-only, changed-file mode only): warn on stderr when a matched listed file is newer on disk than the report file.
- Hygiene: --flag value and --flag=value, duplicate scalar flag is an error, --version reads Package.getImplementationVersion(), --help at top and per-verb.
- Fat jar per build-layout-spec: plain Jar task in cli merging the runtime classpath via zipTree (exactly core), Main-Class set.

## TDD
Drive main() (or a testable runner) end to end against test-fixtures/jacoco/report.xml, asserting exit code, stdout, stderr separately. One test per refusal, one per exit-code path, dash conventions, mtime warning with a touched file.

## Acceptance
- java -jar on the built fat jar runs check against the fixture and exits with the documented code.
- All refusals exit 1 with a one-line message on stderr.
- --json-report - emits parseable JSON only on stdout.

title: Gradle plugin
description:
## Goal
The com.architester.crap4j plugin ships, thin task wrappers over core, config-cache clean.

## Spec
research/gradle-plugin-spec.md, all of it, including the crap-diy.7 amendment (no excludeAnnotations). It supersedes research-findings 5.4. Task semantics tie back to report-and-baseline-spec and junit-sidecar-spec.

## Scope
- Plugin id com.architester.crap4j, extension crap4j per the spec block, conventions threshold 15.0, cap 15, advisory false, attachToCheck false, requireTightBaseline false, formats json and junitXml both true.
- Tasks crapCheck, crapReport, crapBaseline, crapBaselineTighten in the verification group. crapCheck writes all configured reports pass or fail, then fails on violations. crapReport is permanently advisory (JSON advisory true, status pass or advisory). No changed-file mode in the plugin.
- JaCoCo wiring on java projects: apply jacoco if absent, force xml.required true on jacocoTestReport, dependsOn wiring. Non-java projects get no conventions, jacocoXml set explicitly (aggregator case).
- Baseline convention crap4j-baseline.json in projectDir, graceful absence, explicit missing path is an error.
- Per-task output dirs build/reports/crap4j/<taskName>/report.json and junit.xml, each a settable RegularFileProperty. Sidecar suite name is crap4j.<taskName>.
- Config-cache compliant, lazy properties, no Project at execution time, inputs/outputs declared (jacocoXml and baseline @InputFile, reports @OutputFile, baseline tasks own the baseline as output).

## TDD
TestKit functional tests in the functionalTest source set, parameterized with GradleRunner.withGradleVersion over 8.5 and the latest release (build-layout-spec). Fixture projects use test-fixtures/jacoco XMLs as pre-made reports where possible to keep runs fast.

## Acceptance
- Functional tests on both Gradle versions: crapCheck fails a violating build and still writes report files, passes with a covering baseline, crapReport never fails, attachToCheck false keeps check independent and true wires it.
- Second identical run reuses the configuration cache and is up-to-date.
- Regenerated baseline lands at the convention path sorted per spec.

title: Dogfooding baselines and CI workflow
description:
## Goal
open-crap4j gates itself in CI with its own CLI.

## Spec
The Dogfooding and Repo CI sections of research/build-layout-spec.md.

## Scope
- One GitHub Actions workflow, push to main and pull requests, one Linux job, Java 21, Gradle official caching action.
- Steps: build and test everything (unit tests, TestKit matrix, zero-dependency check), then dogfood, run the just-built CLI fat jar once per module against that module's own JaCoCo XML and a committed per-module baseline (per-module gating, ADR 0003).
- Create and commit the three per-module crap4j-baseline.json files (likely empty or tiny on fresh code, run crapBaseline to find out).
- Dogfooding is CI-only, never wired into the local check lifecycle.

## TDD
The workflow is config, the testable part is the dogfood command line. Script it (a small shell step) and run it locally against the built jar before trusting CI. Verify the failure path locally by temporarily lowering a threshold and watching exit 2.

## Acceptance
- The workflow is green on a real PR.
- Locally reproduced dogfood step passes per module, and exits 2 when a threshold is dropped to force a violation.

title: Usage documentation
description:
## Goal
A reader can adopt the tool from the README alone, and the docs never overclaim.

## Sources
research-findings 5.0 (honest cons), 5.2 (threshold coupling), 5.6 (how CRAP fits with other gates), gradle-plugin-spec (multi-module section), cli-spec, mcp-contrast-case-study (real numbers for examples), CONTEXT.md vocabulary.

## Scope
- README: what CRAP is and the formula, quick start for CLI and for the Gradle plugin, baseline adoption workflow (crapBaseline once, commit, gate), tighten versus re-baseline, defaults and the threshold-cap coupling guidance.
- Honest-limits section: bytecode cc is not Checkstyle cc, a stale report describes old code, coverage shows execution not assertion (point at mutation testing), JaCoCo-only.
- CI recipes: GitHub Actions with the JUnit sidecar, changed-file mode via git diff --name-only origin/main... piped to --changed-files -, and the jacoco-report-aggregation combined-gate recipe (one merged XML upstream, one gate reads it, per ADR 0003).
- Adoption guidance for Contrast repos, per-module gating default, what mcp-contrast adoption looks like (two modules, two small baselines).
- Note that exclusions are path globs and class regexes, annotation exclusion is impossible from JaCoCo XML.

## TDD
Docs bead, the test is executability. Every command shown must run verbatim against this repo or test-fixtures/jacoco and produce the output the doc claims.

## Acceptance
- Each documented command executed once, output matches the doc.
- Vocabulary matches CONTEXT.md throughout (slack, tighten, re-baseline, baselined debt).

title: Acceptance: gate mcp-contrast end to end
description:
## Goal
The built v1 gates mcp-contrast end to end. Closing this bead is v1 done (the map's named acceptance test).

## Sources
research/mcp-contrast-case-study.md holds the expected numbers. The repo lives at ~/projects/contrast/mcp-contrast. Work on a local branch there, do not push gate wiring without the user.

## Consumption mechanism
pluginManagement { includeBuild("<path-to-open-crap4j>") } in mcp-contrast settings, decided by crap-diy.7. Zero publishing config needed, publishing is a separate effort (crap-diy.8).

## Scope
- Apply com.architester.crap4j to contrast-mcp-core and contrast-mcp-stdio-app, per-module gating (the default).
- Regenerate coverage (./gradlew test jacocoTestReport), then crapCheck. Expected on core at defaults: 2 violations, RecommendationMarkdownRenderer.registerKnownTags CRAP 38.50 and SearchAppVulnerabilitiesTool.doExecute CRAP 18.52, around 430 methods analyzed. Numbers may drift with upstream commits, investigate any delta beyond drift.
- Walk the lifecycle: crapBaseline, commit locally, crapCheck green with 2 baselined, crapBaselineTighten no-op, requireTightBaseline exercise, advisory exercise.
- CLI pass: crap4j check with --changed-files fed by git diff --name-only against a merge base, and the outdated-report warning by touching a source file.
- JUnit sidecar written and well-formed for both modules (xmllint or equivalent).
- Cross-check: run tools/crap-metrics.py against the same XML and diff its full per-method scores against the JSON report from the Java implementation. Zero disagreements allowed on cc, coverage kind, or crap at two decimals.

## Acceptance
- Both modules gate end to end through the plugin, all lifecycle states exercised.
- CLI changed-file mode works on real git output.
- Python cross-check diff is empty over every scored method in both modules.
- A short findings note is committed to this repo (docs/ or the bead comments) recording actual numbers versus the case study.

title: Parse JaCoCo XML into the method model
description:
## Goal
core parses a JaCoCo XML report into an in-memory model, safely.

## Spec
The input-structure section of research/crap4j-requirements.md, the "What JaCoCo puts in the report" section of research/lambda-folding-spec.md, and the shared conventions of research/report-and-baseline-spec.md (class names stay in slash form verbatim, no dot conversion in core).

## Scope
- JDK-only XML parsing (ADR 0002, no dependencies), XXE-protected.
- CRITICAL: real JaCoCo reports open with <!DOCTYPE report PUBLIC "-//JACOCO//DTD Report 1.1//EN" "report.dtd">. The parser must ACCEPT the DOCTYPE while disabling external entity and external DTD resolution. The common disallow-doctype-decl hardening rejects every real report, do not use it.
- Model: report > package > class (name, sourcefilename) > method (name, descriptor, optional line) with counters (INSTRUCTION, BRANCH, LINE, COMPLEXITY, METHOD) as missed/covered pairs. BRANCH is often absent, line is absent under -g:none.

## TDD
Fixtures are committed at test-fixtures/jacoco/ (report.xml, nd.xml, enum.xml, provenance in its README). Copy them into core test resources. Add one hand-written malicious fixture with an external entity and assert it does not resolve.

## Acceptance
- All three fixtures parse, DOCTYPE and all.
- nd.xml methods have no line and the model represents that as absent, not zero.
- The malicious-entity fixture parses with the entity unresolved or fails cleanly, never fetches or expands.
- Slash-form class names come through verbatim.

title: Lambda folding
description:
## Goal
Synthetic lambda$ methods fold into their enclosing source methods before scoring, exactly per the verified spec.

## Spec
research/lambda-folding-spec.md, all of it. The folding algorithm section is the implementation, the edge case table is the test list.

## Scope
- Regex ^lambda\$(.+)\$(\d+)$ with greedy middle (method names may contain $), new maps to <init>, static maps to <clinit>.
- Overload resolution: largest line <= lambda line, document-order tie-break, document-order fallback when lines are missing.
- Zero candidates keeps the lambda standalone (fail open). Defensive transitive step with a visited set.
- Counter merge: add missed/covered per type (COMPLEXITY, BRANCH, INSTRUCTION, LINE), absent side is 0/0, drop the lambda METHOD counter, merge before any ratio.
- lambda$static$N folds into <clinit> and is skipped with it.
- Never fold across class elements.

## TDD
Every row of the spec edge case table becomes at least one test. Fixtures test-fixtures/jacoco/report.xml (constructors, field and static initializers, overloads, nested, interface default/static, record, anon class, enum), nd.xml (no line attributes, fallback path), enum.xml (JaCoCo self-filtering). Add small hand-written XML for cases the fixtures lack, JDK 8 lambda$null$N, a real method literally named lambda, a method name containing $.

## Acceptance
- Every edge-table row has a passing test.
- A real method named lambda is never folded.
- Folded lambdas are gone from the method list, their counters merged into the target.

title: Scoring engine and exclusions
description:
## Goal
core turns the folded model into scored methods with exclusions applied.

## Spec
The formula in research/crap4j-requirements.md, coverage selection and coupled-threshold warnings in research-findings 5.2 (still authoritative, not superseded), sort order in research/report-and-baseline-spec.md, exclusion defaults per the crap-diy.7 amendment in research/cli-spec.md.

## Scope
- CRAP(m) = cc^2 * (1 - cov)^3 + cc. cc is merged COMPLEXITY missed+covered. Coverage is merged BRANCH ratio when merged BRANCH total > 0, else merged INSTRUCTION ratio. Record coverageKind per method.
- <clinit> is never scored.
- Exclusions: path globs against <package>/<sourcefilename>, class-name regexes against the simple class name, built-in defaults (glob **/generated/**, regexes .*MapperImpl$, ^Dagger.*, ^Hilt_.*, ^AutoValue_.*), one switch disables the defaults. Excluded methods are counted, never scored. There is NO annotation exclusion (crap-diy.7 amendment).
- Deterministic sort: crap descending, ties ascending by class, method, descriptor.
- Coupled-threshold warning computation: unreachable gate when T >= C^2 + C, hidden cap when T < C, with the suggested-pairing texts of text-report-spec S6.

## TDD
Golden numbers from research/mcp-contrast-case-study.md: cc 15 at 0.75 branch scores 18.52 at two decimals, cc 14 at 0.50 scores 38.50, cc 3 at 0.0 instruction scores 12.00, full coverage scores exactly cc. Boundary tests for both warnings at T = C^2 + C and T = C.

## Acceptance
- Golden scores match at full precision rounded to two decimals.
- Exclusion defaults match the amended spec and switch off as one unit.
- Sort is byte-stable across runs.

title: Baseline model, gating, and tighten
description:
## Goal
core reads and writes the baseline file and applies the locked gating rules, including slack and tighten.

## Spec
research/report-and-baseline-spec.md, all of it (baseline file shape, gating rules, epsilon, config mismatch, tighten versus re-baseline, changed-file interactions). It supersedes research-findings 5.5.

## Scope
- Baseline file per spec: formatVersion, toolVersion, generated timestamp, coverageSelection, threshold, complexityCap, entries sorted by class/method/descriptor, each entry class + method + descriptor + crap (two decimals) + complexity.
- Method key is class + method + descriptor, never line numbers.
- Gating rules 1-4 verbatim, both gates ratchet independently, reasons vocabulary crap-over-threshold, complexity-over-cap, crap-regressed, complexity-regressed.
- Epsilon is the fixed constant 0.05, both directions (regression allowance and excess-allowance slack detection). Full-precision current score against stored two-decimal + 0.05. Complexity compares exactly.
- Slack reasons method-gone, under-limits, excess-allowance. requireTightBaseline counts every slack entry as a violation, including summary.violations and top-level status.
- Config mismatch: formatVersion or coverageSelection differs, hard fail demanding re-baseline. threshold or complexityCap differs, warn and gate against current config.
- Tighten never adds an entry, never raises a number, deletes method-gone and under-limits, lowers excess-allowance (crap only past epsilon, complexity on any decrease). Tight means tighten would change nothing.
- Baseline writes (re-baseline and tighten) refuse changed-file mode. Slack detection is disabled in changed-file mode.

## TDD
Table-driven tests over the four gating rules, epsilon boundary cases at exactly +0.05 and just past it in both directions, each slack reason, each mismatch class, tighten idempotence (tighten of a tight baseline is a no-op).

## Acceptance
- Every gating rule and slack reason has tests both sides of its boundary.
- A method baselined at 92 that improves to 50 and drifts back to 90 fails only after a tighten locked in the 50 (the spec's motivating story).
- Baseline serialization round-trips byte-identical for a sorted file.

title: JSON report writer
description:
## Goal
core writes the machine-faithful JSON report, hand-rolled, byte-stable.

## Spec
The JSON report half of research/report-and-baseline-spec.md including all four amendment notes at its top. It supersedes research-findings 5.1. No CSV, no --format none, both are out of scope for v1.

## Scope
- Hand-rolled JSON writing (ADR 0002), correct string escaping.
- Exact top-level shape: formatVersion, toolVersion, status (pass/fail/advisory), advisory, mode, threshold, complexityCap, coverageSelection, baselineFile (omitted only when no baseline configured), summary (methodsAnalyzed, violations, baselinedDebt, slackEntries, excluded), methods, slackBaselineEntries. No timestamp.
- crap two decimals, coverage four-decimal ratio. Per-method omission rules: reasons only on non-ok, baseline only on baselined, line omitted when absent. Top-level fields never omitted.
- status fail appears exactly when the run is enforcing and violations exist. Under requireTightBaseline slack counts in summary.violations, in default warn mode it does not.
- methods sorted crap descending with the identity tie-break, slackBaselineEntries alphabetical.

## TDD
Golden-file byte comparisons built from the scoring and gating engines over scenarios mirroring text-report-spec S1-S8 (first run, baselined, slack warn, slack tight, regression, advisory, clean) plus a changed-file run (slackEntries 0, mode changed-file).

## Acceptance
- Identical input produces a byte-identical file.
- Every scenario golden matches, including field omissions.
- The sidecar invariant precondition holds, summary.violations counts slack exactly when tight mode is on.

title: Text report writer
description:
## Goal
core renders the human report, the eight locked scenarios reproduced to the character.

## Spec
research/text-report-spec.md. Scenarios S1-S8 ARE the spec. Format rules at its top are binding (grouped sections, self-explaining headers, 78-column prose, config echo line, summary block, remedy-naming status lines).

## Scope
- Sections in order: violations, baselined debt, slack. ok methods never print. Columns CRAP (two decimals), cc, coverage percent with kind, ShortClassName.method, violation rows carry (SourceFile.java:line), baselined rows carry the stored allowance.
- Section headers change wording with config (slack under tight mode, violations under advisory), exactly as the scenarios show.
- Summary shows slack-as-violations as "2 violations (2 slack)" in tight mode.
- Coupled-threshold warnings render per S6.
- --show-passing N appends the extra section (crap-diy.4 amendment), N explicit, no default, default output unchanged.
- Remedy wording is producer-aware, Gradle runs name tasks (crapBaselineTighten), CLI runs name verbs (tighten). The producer is a parameter of the renderer.

## TDD
Golden tests for S1 through S8 verbatim (minus the Gradle task banner lines, which belong to Gradle), using the case-study numbers. One test per scenario, plus show-passing on and off, plus CLI-producer remedy wording.

## Acceptance
- Each scenario golden matches character for character within the report body.
- No prose line exceeds 78 columns in any golden.
- S8 clean run prints only echo line, counts, and PASS.

title: JUnit XML sidecar writer
description:
## Goal
core writes the JUnit XML sidecar, the display artifact CI ingests.

## Spec
research/junit-sidecar-spec.md, all of it.

## Scope
- <testsuites> wrapper, one flat <testsuite> named crap4j.<producer>, counts tests/failures/skipped, errors always 0, time 0 everywhere, no timestamp, byte-identical for identical input.
- One testcase per scored method (mirrors the JSON methods array and its order) plus one per slack baseline entry in whole-repo mode (alphabetical, after methods).
- Status mapping table verbatim: violation is failure, baselined is skipped, slack is skipped in warn mode and failure in tight mode. Violations render as failure even in advisory runs.
- classname dot form with $ kept, name is method name plus pretty parameter list decoded from the JVM descriptor (arrays with [], no return types), collision fallback appends the descriptor, slack rows get the [slack] suffix. Descriptor decoding is real work, test it hard.
- failure type carries the primary reason, messages reuse the text-report vocabulary and numbers, producer-aware remedies.
- Only <failure>, never <error>. Self-closing elements with message attributes, standard XML escaping (<init> etc). Always written when enabled, even empty (tests="0").

## TDD
The invariant implementers test: the <failure> row count equals summary.violations in every mode. Assert it across all golden scenarios (S1-S8 equivalents, changed-file, advisory, tight). Golden files for the document shape. Descriptor-decoding unit tests: (Ljava/lang/String;I)V, arrays, nested class parameters, <init>.

## Acceptance
- Invariant holds in every scenario.
- Goldens byte-match, escaping correct.
- Overload pair stays two distinct rows, forced collision appends descriptors.

title: Changed-file mode
description:
## Goal
core restricts analysis to a supplied file list with the locked matching rules.

## Spec
The changed-file sections of research/cli-spec.md and research/report-and-baseline-spec.md, plus requirements feature 4. The tool never computes the list itself.

## Scope
- Suffix match: a listed path matches a class when it ends with <package>/<sourceFile>. Path boundary rule, the character before the suffix must be / or the listed path equals the suffix exactly (mycom/example/Foo.java must NOT match com/example/Foo.java).
- Default package: match string is bare Foo.java, only the equality arm matches it.
- Backslashes normalize to slashes before matching.
- Lines matching nothing count as skipped. An empty changed set is a clean no-op, exit 0 semantics.
- In changed-file mode slack detection is off (slackEntries 0, slackBaselineEntries empty), baseline gating still applies to analyzed methods, report mode field says changed-file.

## TDD
Table-driven matcher tests: exact suffix, longer prefix with / boundary, the mycom counter-example, default package hit and miss, backslash input, README.md skipped. Integration test over test-fixtures/jacoco/report.xml slicing to one class.

## Acceptance
- Every boundary case above passes.
- Raw git diff --name-only style paths (src/main/java/...) match verbatim.
- Empty set analyzes nothing and reports a clean pass.

title: open-crap4j design and implementation plan
description:
## Destination

The design is locked and an ordered implementation plan exists as br issues, with nothing left to decide before build sessions execute. The plan names mcp-contrast as its acceptance test, a built v1 must gate that repo end to end.

## Notes

- Domain, a CRAP metric gate for Java plus Gradle plus JaCoCo. Read research/crap4j-research-findings.md before working any ticket, it holds the studied design. research/crap4j-requirements.md holds the original requirements. research/mcp-contrast-case-study.md holds real-world numbers.
- Skills, use /grilling and /domain-modeling on every HITL ticket. The implementation plan mandates TDD.
- Glossary lives in CONTEXT.md. Keep it current as terms sharpen.

Settled during charting (2026-08-12):

- Destination form, plan not build. Execution happens off-map via the plan's beads.
- v1 scope, per-method CRAP with lambda folding, whole-repo and changed-file modes, baseline gating, complexity cap, text and JSON output, JUnit XML sidecar, CLI plus Gradle plugin.
- Consumption, local first (mavenLocal or includeBuild). Public publishing deferred.
- Identity, personal OSS. License Apache-2.0. Group com.architester (the user owns architester.com), base package com.architester.crap4j, project name open-crap4j.
- Build, Gradle with Kotlin DSL, Java 17 bytecode target, toolchain 21.
- Zero runtime dependencies in core and gradle-plugin.
- crapCheck attaches to the Gradle check lifecycle only by opt-in.
- The baseline grandfathers both CRAP and complexity-cap violations through one mechanism.
- Defaults, CRAP threshold 15, complexity cap 15, coupled-threshold warnings per research doc section 5.2.

## Decisions so far

- [Validate lambda folding against real JaCoCo reports](crap-diy.2) — grammar confirmed, spec at research/lambda-folding-spec.md. Four amendments to the draft rules, transitive nested-lambda names never occur on JDK 9+, constructor line collisions need a document-order tie-break, the fold regex must require the trailing $digits, and lambda$static$N folds into <clinit> and is skipped.
- [Lock the JSON report schema and baseline file format](crap-diy.1) — spec at research/report-and-baseline-spec.md, supersedes research-findings 5.1 (json) and 5.5. Three-value report status (pass, fail, advisory), reasons vocabulary, slash-form class names verbatim from JaCoCo, spelled-out field names, crap at two decimals with a fixed 0.05 epsilon, baseline ratchets crap and complexity independently, prune lowers but never raises, baseline writes are whole-repo only, formatVersion bumps on meaning changes only. Vocabulary amended by crap-diy.5, prune is now tighten, regenerate is re-baseline, stale is slack.
- [Lock the Gradle plugin DSL and task wiring](crap-diy.5) — spec at research/gradle-plugin-spec.md, supersedes research-findings 5.4. Plugin id com.architester.crap4j, extension crap4j, tasks crapCheck, crapReport, crapBaseline, crapBaselineTighten, Gradle 8.5+, config-cache compliant. Single jacocoXml input, one gate reads one report, aggregation stays upstream in JaCoCo (ADR 0003), per-module gating by default. No changed-file mode in the plugin. Renamed stale to slack with the requireTightBaseline switch, amended into the report spec, glossary, and JSON field names. Surfaced the JUnit sidecar semantics ticket.
- [Prototype the text report and warning output](crap-diy.3) — text output locked, spec at research/text-report-spec.md. Grouped sections (violations, baselined debt, slack), ok methods never print, every section header explains itself in one line under 78 columns, status line names the remedy. Amended the report spec, under requireTightBaseline slack counts in summary.violations. Surfaced a worst-passing flag question onto the CLI ticket.
- [Lock the CLI surface](crap-diy.4) — spec at research/cli-spec.md, supersedes research-findings 5.3. Command crap4j, a zero-dependency executable fat jar with four subcommands mirroring the Gradle tasks (check, report, baseline, tighten). Exit codes 0/1/2 with exit 2 aligned to status fail, --require-tight-baseline errors when combined with --changed-files, changed-file lists suffix-match so raw git diff --name-only output works verbatim, outdated-report warning in changed-file mode, --show-passing N settles the crap-diy.3 worst-passing question, dedicated output flags (--json-report, --junit-report) with - conventions replace --format/--output. Amended the report and text-report specs.
- [Decide the build layout for this repo](crap-diy.6) — spec at research/build-layout-spec.md, supersedes research-findings 5.4's implementation notes on layout. Three modules (core, cli, gradle-plugin) in one Gradle multi-project build, artifacts crap4j-*, buildSrc convention plugin, one shared version from 0.1.0 read via Implementation-Version, CLI fat jar is a plain Jar task (no Shadow), ADR 0002 enforced by a check-wired task that fails on any non-project runtime artifact, JUnit 5 + AssertJ, TestKit matrix (8.5 + latest) parameterized inside the tests, dogfooding via the CLI fat jar per module in one minimal GitHub Actions workflow (build+test then dogfood, CI-only).
- [Lock the JUnit XML sidecar semantics](crap-diy.9) — spec at research/junit-sidecar-spec.md. One testcase per scored method plus one per slack baseline entry, failure rows equal summary.violations in every mode, baselined debt and warn-mode slack render as skipped, tight-mode slack fails, advisory keeps red rows (the exit code carries the gate), dot-form names with pretty parameter lists and a [slack] suffix, one flat suite named crap4j.<producer>, failure only (never error), time 0 and no timestamps, always written including empty runs, messages reuse the text-report vocabulary. Questioned and upheld the crapCheck/crapReport two-task split.
- [Author the ordered implementation plan](crap-diy.7) — plan authored as epic crap-0w4 (open-crap4j v1 build), 14 dependency-ordered ready-for-agent beads from scaffold to the terminal bead that gates mcp-contrast end to end, TDD mandated throughout. Dropped annotation exclusion from v1 (JaCoCo XML carries no annotation data, ADR 0001 makes the flag unimplementable, amended into the CLI and Gradle specs), acceptance consumption is pluginManagement includeBuild, the clean-room lambda fixtures are committed at test-fixtures/jacoco, and tools/crap-metrics.py is the independent cross-check the acceptance bead diffs against.

## Not yet specified

Nothing. All fog graduated, usage documentation became a plan bead and the cross-check-harness question was decided (committed as tools/crap-metrics.py, used by the acceptance bead).

## Out of scope

- Maven plugin, CSV output, CRAP-load and project-summary metrics, churn weighting, mutation-testing integration. v2 candidates, none block v1.
- Executing the public release. The publishing ticket decides coordinates and process only.
- Building v1 itself. Execution belongs to the plan this map produces.

title: Lock the JSON report schema and baseline file format
description:
## Question

Final field names and structure for the JSON report and the baseline file. Includes the status vocabulary, rounding and epsilon rules, format version semantics, prune versus regenerate semantics, and how baseline gating interacts with changed-file mode. Research doc sections 5.1 and 5.5 are the draft to confirm or amend.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text: Resolved. Full spec at research/report-and-baseline-spec.md, which supersedes research-findings sections 5.1 (json) and 5.5. Headline decisions: three-value report status (pass, fail, advisory) so grep for fail never false-alarms on advisory runs; method status ok/baselined/violation plus a reasons vocabulary (crap-over-threshold, complexity-over-cap, crap-regressed, complexity-regressed); baseline entries store crap and complexity and both ratchet independently; class names slash-form verbatim from JaCoCo in both files; fields spelled out (complexity, coverage, descriptor, sourceFile); crap two decimals, coverage ratio four decimals, fixed epsilon 0.05 (a constant, not a setting); stale entries reported as a top-level list plus count with reasons method-gone/under-limits; prune deletes stale and ratchets improved entries down, never adds or raises; regenerate re-admits worsened debt by design; threshold/cap mismatch warns, formatVersion/coverageSelection mismatch hard-fails; changed-file mode gates normally but disables stale detection and refuses baseline writes; formatVersion bumps on meaning changes only, additive optional fields (e.g. a future per-method module field for crap-diy.5) never bump. CSV and CRAP-load stayed out of scope per the map.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text: Amended by crap-diy.5 (2026-08-13), vocabulary only, mechanics unchanged. prune→tighten, regenerate→re-baseline, stale→slack. JSON fields staleEntries/staleBaselineEntries renamed to slackEntries/slackBaselineEntries (no code or readers existed, formatVersion stays 1), slack gains an excess-allowance reason guarded by the epsilon, and strict mode is requireTightBaseline. See the amendment note in research/report-and-baseline-spec.md and research/gradle-plugin-spec.md.

title: Validate lambda folding against real JaCoCo reports
description:
## Question

Do the folding rules survive contact with real reports? Verify javac lambda naming (lambda$name$N) on Java 17 and 21 against mcp-contrast's jacocoTestReport.xml and JaCoCo documentation or source. Cover overload disambiguation by start line, nested lambdas, lambdas in constructors and static initializers, interface default methods, records, and switch expression desugaring. Confirm class plus method name plus JVM descriptor is a stable baseline key under all of these. Deliverable, a folding spec with an edge-case table.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text: Resolved. Full spec at research/lambda-folding-spec.md. Confirmed against mcp-contrast XML, javap on JDK 21, a live JaCoCo 0.8.12 run, and javac plus JaCoCo source. The lambda$<name>$<n> grammar holds (new for constructors and field initializers, static for static initializers). JaCoCo keeps lambda$ methods as separate method elements and filters other synthetics. The closest-not-greater overload rule resolved all 12 real overloaded fold targets. class+name+descriptor is a stable baseline key, and folding is what makes it stable. Four amendments to the draft rules: (1) javac never emits nested-lambda names, JDK 9+ names them after the enclosing source method, so transitive resolution stays only as a defensive no-op and JDK 8 era lambda$null$N is handled as a missing-target fallback. (2) Constructor line attributes collide when field initializers exist, add a document-order tie-break. (3) The fold regex must require the trailing $<digits>, a real source method named lambda exists in the wild. (4) lambda$static$N folds into <clinit> and is skipped with it.

title: Prototype the text report and warning output
description:
## Question

What should a human see? Mock the text table, the summary block, baseline warnings, slack-entry notes, and the coupled-threshold warnings, using real numbers from the mcp-contrast case study. React and iterate until it reads right. Vocabulary per the crap-diy.5 amendments, slack and tighten, not stale and prune.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text:
Resolved by prototype iteration with the user, spec locked at research/text-report-spec.md.

The mock renders eight scenarios with real mcp-contrast numbers, first run fails, baseline adopted, slack appears, tight required, regression, coupled-threshold warnings, advisory, clean pass. Decisions locked:

- Grouped sections (Violations, Baselined debt, Slack in the baseline), ok methods never print. Status-column table rejected as default.
- Every section header carries a one-line plain-language explanation of what the category means and whether it acts on the build. User feedback drove this, the bare labels did not explain themselves.
- Explanatory lines never wrap, max 78 columns. Only data columns may run wider.
- Columns, CRAP two decimals exact, cc, coverage percent with kind, ShortClass.method. Violations carry file:line, baselined rows carry the stored allowance.
- Summary block plus a status line that names the remedy.
- Under requireTightBaseline slack counts in summary.violations, shown as N violations (N slack). Amended into research/report-and-baseline-spec.md.
- Corrected the case study rounding, doExecute is 18.52 at two decimals, not 18.50.

Surfaced for crap-diy.4, whether a flag exposes worst-passing methods (top-N or show-passing).

title: Lock the CLI surface
description:
## Question

Final flags, exit codes, stdin handling for the changed-file list, stale-report warning behavior, and how the CLI ships (fat jar). Research doc section 5.3 is the draft.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text:
Constraints from crap-diy.5 (research/gradle-plugin-spec.md):
1. Single --report, not repeatable. One analysis reads one report everywhere, aggregation stays upstream in JaCoCo (ADR 0003). Drop the repeatable flag from the 5.3 draft.
2. Vocabulary changed, prune→tighten, regenerate→re-baseline, stale→slack. The Gradle strict switch is requireTightBaseline, derive the CLI spelling from it (an earlier --fail-on-stale suggestion is superseded).
3. Slack detection is disabled in changed-file mode, so decide whether the require-tight flag combined with --changed-files is a no-op or a usage error.
4. Baseline write and tighten verbs need CLI spellings too (--write-baseline exists in the draft, tighten does not).

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text: From crap-diy.3, the text spec hides ok methods entirely. Decide whether the CLI offers a flag to show worst-passing methods (top-N or a show-passing switch), see the rejected alternate at the bottom of research/text-report-spec.md.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text:
Resolved, spec at research/cli-spec.md, supersedes research doc 5.3.

Command is crap4j, an executable fat jar (java -jar, Java 17+), zero dependencies including hand-rolled arg parsing. Four subcommands mirror the Gradle tasks, check, report, baseline, tighten. Exit codes 0 pass/advisory/no-op, 1 usage or input error, 2 violations, aligned with status: fail. Strict switch spells --require-tight-baseline and combining it with --changed-files is a usage error on check and report both. Baseline and tighten refuse --changed-files. --report is required with no default path. Changed-file lists come one path per line from file or stdin (-), matched by path-boundary-safe suffix match so raw git diff --name-only output works verbatim. Outdated-report warning fires in changed-file mode only, stderr, when a matched listed file is newer than the report. Worst-passing view ships as --show-passing N, opt-in text section, resolving the crap-diy.3 question. Dedicated output flags replace --format/--output, text always on stdout, --json-report path or - (stdout, suppresses text), --junit-report path. Baseline path convention mirrors Gradle graceful absence. Hygiene, --flag=value accepted, duplicate scalar flags error, per-verb --help, --version.

Note for crap-diy.9, the --junit-report flag spelling and verb placement (check and report) are decided here, sidecar semantics stay with that ticket.

Amended research/report-and-baseline-spec.md (deferred CLI questions) and research/text-report-spec.md (worst-passing alternate adopted as opt-in flag). Glossary gained outdated report.

title: Lock the Gradle plugin DSL and task wiring
description:
## Question

Final extension properties, task names and behavior (crapCheck, crapReport, crapBaseline), attachToCheck wiring, configuration-cache compliance, and multi-module aggregation semantics (root-project application, duplicate classes across modules, merging multiple reports). Research doc section 5.4 is the draft.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text:
Resolved. Spec locked at research/gradle-plugin-spec.md, supersedes research-findings section 5.4.

- Plugin id com.architester.crap4j, extension crap4j { }, minimum Gradle 8.5, configuration-cache compliant (lazy properties, declared inputs and outputs, no subproject crawling).
- Tasks, all in the verification group. crapCheck gates and always writes the configured reports, check depends on it only via attachToCheck. crapReport is the never-failing twin, its JSON is a permanently advisory run (advisory: true, status pass or advisory), forced by the locked rule that fail appears only when the build really failed. crapBaseline writes the baseline, first run or re-baseline. crapBaselineTighten removes slack.
- Single jacocoXml input (RegularFileProperty). One gate reads one report, coverage merging stays upstream in JaCoCo (ADR 0003). Per-module gating is the default, a combined gate is user wiring via jacoco-report-aggregation. The reserved per-method module field stays unwritten in v1.
- JaCoCo auto-wiring, apply the plugin if absent, force xml.required, dependsOn the report task.
- Baseline convention crap4j-baseline.json in the module folder with graceful absence, an explicitly configured missing path is an error.
- No changed-file mode in the v1 plugin, the CLI owns it.
- Outputs, text summary always on the console, json and junitXml on by default, per-task directories build/reports/crap4j/<taskName>/ with settable RegularFileProperty paths.
- Exclusion knobs carried from the draft unchanged (excludes, excludeClasses, excludeAnnotations, useDefaultExclusions=true).
- Vocabulary renames amended into report-and-baseline-spec.md and CONTEXT.md, prune→tighten, regenerate→re-baseline, stale→slack, strict switch requireTightBaseline, JSON fields slackEntries/slackBaselineEntries, new reason excess-allowance, epsilon-guarded so tight means exactly that tighten would change nothing.

Surfaced crap-diy.9 (JUnit sidecar semantics, blocks crap-diy.7) and constraint comments on crap-diy.4 and crap-diy.3.

title: Decide the build layout for this repo
description:
## Question

Module structure (core, cli, gradle-plugin), single Gradle build versus composite for the plugin, TestKit setup, version management, and how zero-runtime-dependency stays enforced.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text: Resolved. Spec at research/build-layout-spec.md. Three modules (core, cli, gradle-plugin) in one Gradle multi-project build, no composite. Artifacts crap4j-core/-cli/-gradle-plugin via base.archivesName. buildSrc convention plugin holds toolchain 21 / release 17, JUnit 5 + AssertJ, JaCoCo with XML forced on, and a zero-dep check that fails check when runtimeClasspath resolves any non-project artifact (ADR 0002 becomes a build guarantee). CLI fat jar is a plain Jar task merging core, no Shadow. One shared version in gradle.properties from 0.1.0, manifests carry Implementation-Version, crap4j --version reads it. TestKit via java-gradle-plugin functionalTest source set, Gradle matrix (8.5 + latest) parameterized inside the tests. Dogfooding, CI runs the just-built CLI fat jar per module against each module's JaCoCo XML and committed baseline, CI-only, never in local check. Repo CI, one GitHub Actions workflow (push to main + PRs), single Linux job, Java 21, gradle caching action, build+test then dogfood.

title: Author the ordered implementation plan
description:
## Question

Turn the locked specs into dependency-ordered br beads, each executable in one session, each naming its TDD fixtures and acceptance checks, ending with a bead that gates mcp-contrast end to end. Closing this ticket closes the map.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text:
Resolved. The plan exists as epic crap-0w4 (open-crap4j v1 build), 14 dependency-ordered beads, each sized to one session, each labeled ready-for-agent, each naming its specs, TDD fixtures, and acceptance checks. br ready hands build sessions the next bead, starting at crap-0w4.1 (scaffold). The terminal bead crap-0w4.14 gates mcp-contrast end to end, per the map's destination.

Order: scaffold -> XML parser -> lambda folding -> scoring and exclusions -> baseline gating and tighten -> {json writer, text writer, junit sidecar, changed-file mode} -> {CLI, Gradle plugin} -> {dogfood CI, docs} -> mcp-contrast acceptance.

Decisions made while authoring, all recorded in the beads and specs:

1. DROPPED --exclude-annotation / excludeAnnotations from v1. JaCoCo XML carries no annotation data, so annotation-based exclusion is impossible under ADR 0001. JaCoCo itself filters CLASS/RUNTIME-retention *Generated annotations, SOURCE-retention javax/jakarta @Generated is invisible to everyone. Path globs and class regexes are the exclusion tools, defaults restated explicitly. Amended into research/cli-spec.md and research/gradle-plugin-spec.md with dated notes. This corrects locked specs, flag if you disagree.
2. Acceptance consumption is pluginManagement includeBuild in mcp-contrast, zero publishing config, publishing stays with crap-diy.8.
3. The clean-room lambda fixtures were rescued from /tmp before they evaporate, committed at test-fixtures/jacoco (report.xml, nd.xml, enum.xml plus sources and a provenance README). They carry the real JaCoCo DOCTYPE, and the parser bead warns that naive XXE hardening rejects it.
4. /tmp/crap-metrics.py is committed as tools/crap-metrics.py, the independent cross-check the acceptance bead diffs the Java implementation against over every scored method.
5. The docs fog graduated into bead crap-0w4.13 (usage documentation), execution work, not a map decision.

The map is not closed by this ticket alone, Decide the publishing path (crap-diy.8) is now unblocked and is the last frontier ticket.

title: Decide the publishing path
description:
## Question

Coordinates under com.architester (DNS TXT verification of architester.com for Maven Central), Central Portal and Gradle Plugin Portal accounts, signing, and release automation. Decide only, execution is out of scope for this map. Best worked after v1 proves out on mcp-contrast.

title: Lock the JUnit XML sidecar semantics
description:
## Question

What does the JUnit XML sidecar contain? What maps to a testcase (one per scored method, or violations only), what counts as a failure, how baselined debt and slack entries render, and what advisory mode does to it (all-pass, or failures that CI shows without gating). Shared by crapCheck, crapReport, and the CLI, so the mapping is one spec. Surfaced by crap-diy.5, which fixed only its file location (build/reports/crap4j/<taskName>/junit.xml, on by default in Gradle).

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text: From crap-diy.3, under requireTightBaseline slack entries count in summary.violations but they are baseline entries, not methods, so the violations count can exceed the count of methods with status violation. Decide whether a slack entry becomes a failing testcase in the JUnit sidecar under tight mode. See the crap-diy.3 amendment in research/report-and-baseline-spec.md.

comments.author: Chris Edwards
comments.text: Resolved, spec at research/junit-sidecar-spec.md. One testcase per scored method mirroring the JSON methods array, plus one per slack baseline entry in whole-repo mode. Palette rule, a failure row appears exactly when the entry counts in summary.violations, so baselined debt and warn-mode slack render as skipped-with-message, and tight-mode slack renders as a failure (this answers the crap-diy.3 comment on this ticket). Advisory keeps red rows, the exit code carries the gate, which keeps crapReport's sidecar useful for rollout. Dot-form classname, pretty parameter lists in name, [slack] suffix keeps slack rows from colliding with method rows. One flat suite named crap4j.<producer>. Only failure, never error, time 0, no timestamps, always-written including empty runs, messages reuse the text-report vocabulary. Side outcome, the session questioned and upheld the crapCheck/crapReport two-task split (JaCoCo pattern), no spec change. Amended pointers in cli-spec, gradle-plugin-spec, report-and-baseline-spec, glossary gained JUnit sidecar.
